title: complete
description: Result of `stride complete <id> [activity]`. `rest` marks the bare form, allowed only for rest days. Both forms report what the call DESTROYED: `replaced_activity` and `released_substitute` are always present, 0 meaning nothing was.

replaced_activity.description: The activity whose completion of this session was REPLACED by this call, or 0 if none was. `complete` on a session that is already `done` overwrites the link — it is the documented repair for a mis-linked completion, and `skip`'s own refusal message names it as such — but until #258 the payload was indistinguishable from a first-time completion, so a typo'd session id rewrote real history and reported plain success. Always present rather than optional: a consumer deciding whether history was rewritten must not have to tell an absent key from a zero. 0 is a safe sentinel for the same reason `ftp_used > 0` is the house discriminator (AGENTS.md) — this names an activity id, and no activity has id 0.

released_substitute.description: The activity that was standing in for this session as a substitute and no longer is, or 0 if none was. `complete` NULLs `substitute_activity_id` on both forms, so completing a session that had been `skipped` with a substitute destroys the only record that the athlete did that activity in its place. Same name and meaning as `skip`'s key. Silent when the substitute IS the completing activity: that is a promotion, not a loss, and the caller still holds the link.

released_substitute_of.description: A DIFFERENT session whose display-dead substitute link this activity was stolen from. Optional, unlike the two above: it reports an incidental side effect on another row, meaningful only when it happened, and answers no question a consumer must ask on every completion.
